bibl.title: Massively parallel digital transcriptional profiling of single cells

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: 3' mRNA counting of tens of thousands of individual cells in parallel - and, separately, telling whose cells they are from the same reads
span.quote: To overcome these challenges, we developed a droplet-based system that enables 3′ messenger RNA (mRNA) digital counting of thousands of single cells. Approximately 50% of cells loaded into the system can be captured, and up to eight samples can be processed in parallel per run. Reverse transcription takes place inside each droplet, and barcoded complementary DNAs (cDNAs) are amplified in bulk. The resulting libraries then undergo Illumina short-read sequencing.

span.label: whether tens of thousands of single cells can be captured and barcoded without custom microfluidics or plate sorting, and at what multiplet, capture and conversion rates
span.quote: However, previously described scRNA-seq methods face practical challenges when scaling to tens of thousands of cells or when it is necessary to capture as many cells as possible from a limited sample. Commercially available, microfluidic-based approaches have limited throughput. Plate-based methods often require time-consuming fluorescence-activated cell sorting (FACS) into many plates that must be processed separately. Droplet-based techniques have enabled processing of tens of thousands of cells in a single experiment, but current approaches require generation of custom microfluidic devices and reagents.

span.label: a gel-bead-in-emulsion platform capturing ~50% of loaded cells across 8 parallel channels, with its multiplet rate, cross-talk and conversion efficiency each measured against a control of known composition; plus a de novo SNV method that resolves transplant chimerism without either genotype
span.quote: Current clinical chimerism tests have a number of limitations, namely (1) the flow-sorted cell populations are limited by cell surface markers, (2) only populations with sufficient cell counts can be used for PCR assays and (3) they are not intended for the detection of minimal residual disease. Here we present a simple method that addresses these limitations, resolves host and donor chimerism at single-cell resolution and enables extensive characterization of cell subtypes by integrating scRNA-seq with de novo SNV calling.

span.label: method
span.quote: To overcome these challenges, we developed a droplet-based system that enables 3′ messenger RNA (mRNA) digital counting of thousands of single cells. Approximately 50% of cells loaded into the system can be captured, and up to eight samples can be processed in parallel per run. Reverse transcription takes place inside each droplet, and barcoded complementary DNAs (cDNAs) are amplified in bulk. The resulting libraries then undergo Illumina short-read sequencing.

span.label: transcriptomic heterogeneity that population-averaged measurement hides, and the droplet-level artefacts - multiplets, barcode cross-talk, technical variance - that appear once you measure cells one at a time
span.quote: Last, the mean fraction of UMI counts from the other species was 0.9% in both human and mouse GEMs, indicating a low level of cross-talk between cell barcodes (Online Supplementary Methods).

span.label: cells loaded at limiting dilution into gel-bead emulsions, reverse transcribed in droplet with a 14 bp barcode and a 10 bp UMI, amplified in bulk, sequenced short-read, and processed by Cell Ranger into a gene-barcode matrix
span.term: cells loaded at limiting dilution into gel-bead emulsions, reverse transcribed in droplet with a 14 bp barcode and a 10 bp UMI, amplified in bulk, sequenced short-read, and processed by Cell Ranger into a gene-barcode matrix
span.quote: Within each microfluidic channel, ∼100,000 GEMs are formed per ∼6-min run, encapsulating thousands of cells in GEMs. Cells are loaded at a limiting dilution to minimize co-occurrence of multiple cells in the same GEM.

span.label: cells are loaded far below one per droplet so that two rarely share a barcode; the same dilution that suppresses multiplets is what throws away the cells that are never captured, so the multiplet rate and the capture rate are two readings of one loading decision
span.term: limiting dilution as the price of purity
span.quote: Within each microfluidic channel, ∼100,000 GEMs are formed per ∼6-min run, encapsulating thousands of cells in GEMs. Cells are loaded at a limiting dilution to minimize co-occurrence of multiple cells in the same GEM.

span.label: synthetic RNAs at a known concentration are loaded in place of cells, so every difference between the expected and observed counts must come from the instrument - the variance that remains is technical by construction rather than by argument
span.term: a droplet with no biology in it
span.quote: The ERCC experiments also allowed us to estimate the relative proportion of biological and technical variation. Since ERCCs are in solution, they do not introduce biological variation related to differences in cell size, RNA content or transcriptional activity. Thus, technical variation is the only source of variation.

span.label: a barcode carrying substantial human and mouse counts can only have held two cells, so mixing species converts an invisible failure into a countable one - and the count must then be doubled, because same-species doublets are equally likely and leave no trace
span.term: two species as a doublet detector
span.quote: In the mouse and human mixing experiments, multiplet rate was defined as twice the rate of cell barcodes with significant UMI counts from both mouse and human, where top 1% of UMI counts was considered significant. The extent of barcode crosstalk was assessed by the fraction of mouse reads in human barcodes, or vice versa.

span.label: the ~250 nt of cDNA that gives an expression count also carries sequence variants, so each cell has an expression identity and a genotype identity from the same reads; agreement between them is evidence neither could give alone
span.term: identity read twice from one molecule
span.quote: In the 1:1 mixed sample, 45% 293T cells primarily (96%) harbored 293T-enriched SNVs, whereas 50% Jurkat cells primarily (94%) harbored Jurkat-enriched SNVs (Fig. 2f and Supplementary Data 2). Jurkat and 293T cells inferred from marker-based analysis are 99% consistent with SNV-based assignment.

span.label: an observed barcode one Hamming step from known sequences is reassigned by posterior probability from base qualities and the overall barcode count distribution, above 0.975, with lexical order as the stated tie-break rather than a silent one
span.term: posterior correction of a barcode without a whitelist match
span.quote: All of the known listed of barcodes that are 1-Hamming-distance away from an observed barcode are considered. Then, the posterior probability that the observed barcode was produced by a sequencing error is computed, given the base qualities of the observed barcode and the prior probability of observing the candidate barcode (taken from the overall barcode count distribution). If the posterior probability for any candidate barcode is at least 0.975, then the barcode is corrected to the candidate barcode with the highest posterior probability. If all candidate sequences are equally probable, then the one appearing first by lexical order is picked.

span.label: the level of detection of the genotype method is given as 3% in Results and as 4% of 6,000 cells in Methods, for the same in silico mixing experiment, and the two are never reconciled
span.quote: Our method was able to identify minor genotypes as low as 3% at >95% sensitivity and PPV (Fig. 4a,b). A minor population could not be detected when the mixed ratio was below 3%

span.label: the same discrepancy, from the Methods side - K=1 is selected when the mixture fraction is below 4% of 6,000 cells
span.quote: Selecting K=1 indicates that the mixture fraction is below the level of detection of the method, which in in silico mixing experiments was determined to be 4% of 6,000 cells.

span.label: multiplets of identical or highly similar cell types cannot be detected by any of the measures used here, and the authors say more sophisticated methods will be required
span.quote: Cells in cluster 10 express markers of B, T and dendritic cells, suggesting a likely cluster of multiplets (Fig. 3b,c). The size of the cluster suggests the multiplets comprises mostly B:dendritic and B:T:dendritic cells (Supplementary Methods). With ∼9k cells recovered per channel, we expect a ∼9% multiplet rate and that the majority of multiplets would only contain T cells. More sophisticated methods will be required to detect multiplets from identical or highly similar cell types.

span.label: a 15-20% error in the cell counts feeds directly into the capture efficiency, and the authors name it as a source of the variability in that figure
span.quote: It is worth noting that there is a 15–20% error in cell counts, which could account for at least some of the variability in the calculated efficiencies.

span.label: imaged multiple-encapsulation was 16% higher than the Poisson expectation, ascribed to subsampling error or to cell-cell clumping seen during the manual count
span.quote: The results indicate an approximate adherence to a Poisson distribution. However, the percentage of multiple cell encapsulations was 16% higher than the expected value, possibly due to subsampling error or to cell–cell interactions (some two-cell clumps were observed during the manual count) (Supplementary Fig. 1b).

span.label: classification blurred the boundaries between T-cell subpopulations, with part of the inferred CD4+ naive population classified as CD8+ T cells
span.quote: Cell classification was largely consistent with previously described marker-based classification, although the boundaries among some of the T-cell subpopulations were blurred. Namely, part of the inferred CD4+ naive T population was classified as CD8+ T cells.

span.label: the transplant work is a proof of principle on BMMCs from two patients
span.quote: While this proof-of-principle study only contained BMMCs from two transplant patients, it highlights the potential clinical impact of the technology, and lays the foundation for more extensive studies involving larger numbers of patient samples.

span.label: the unexpected absence of monocytes after transplant is reported without explanation and left for further study
span.quote: Third, monocytes are abundant in both AML patients before transplant (10% and 25% in AML027 and AML035 respectively), but are not detectable after transplant (Fig. 5b). Monocytes have been previously identified in post-transplant samples, and the unexpected monocytopenia needs to be followed up with additional studies.

span.label: the GemCode gel-bead-in-emulsion barcoding platform, carried from genome haplotyping, structural variant analysis and de novo genome assembly into single-cell RNA counting
span.quote: The scRNA-seq microfluidics platform builds on the GemCode technology, which has been used for genome haplotyping, structural variant analysis and de novo assembly of a human genome.

span.label: the two-genome mixture model with a Gibbs sampler and Stephens relabelling, carried from mixture-model statistics into deciding which transplanted cells are whose
span.quote: While previous studies have used existing SNVs from DNA sequencing or large-scale copy number changes in the transcriptome data to distinguish cells by genotype, these methods cannot be applied to transplant samples where donor and host genotype is not known a priori, and when donor and host are closely matched in genotype.

span.label: a mixture of ~1,200 human 293T and ~1,200 mouse 3T3 cells loaded together, so that a droplet holding two cells leaves a two-genome barcode behind it
span.note: eliminates: multiplets and barcode cross-talk being invisible - in a single-species run a doublet and a large cell produce the same data, and neither rate can be read · outcome: held
span.quote: To assess the technical performance of our system, we loaded a mixture of ∼1,200 human (293T) and ∼1,200 mouse (3T3) cells and sequenced the library on the Illumina NextSeq 500 to yield ∼100k reads per cell.

span.label: a cell titration across six different cell loads, recovering 1,200 to 9,500 cells
span.note: eliminates: the 1.6% figure being a fixed property of the instrument - if the rate did not track the load, the mechanism would not be Poisson co-encapsulation at all · outcome: held
span.quote: A cell titration experiment across six different cell loads showed a linear relationship between the multiplet rate and the number of recovered cells ranging from 1,200 to 9,500 (Supplementary Fig. 1a). The multiplet rate and trend are consistent with Poisson loading of cells, and have been validated by independent imaging experiments (Supplementary Methods and Supplementary Fig. 1b).

span.label: high-speed imaging of every GEM as it formed, with ~28k frames counted by hand, as a measurement of cell occupancy that does not pass through sequencing
span.note: eliminates: the Poisson loading claim resting on the same data it explains - the imaging can disagree with the sequencing, and it does, by 16% · outcome: partial
span.quote: The results indicate an approximate adherence to a Poisson distribution. However, the percentage of multiple cell encapsulations was 16% higher than the expected value, possibly due to subsampling error or to cell–cell interactions (some two-cell clumps were observed during the manual count) (Supplementary Fig. 1b).

span.label: ERCC synthetic spike-in RNAs at known concentration loaded into GEMs in place of cells, in two mixes and two dilutions
span.note: eliminates: biological variation as a contributor to the measured variance, and the conversion efficiency being inferred from data with no known answer · outcome: held
span.quote: The ERCC experiments also allowed us to estimate the relative proportion of biological and technical variation. Since ERCCs are in solution, they do not introduce biological variation related to differences in cell size, RNA content or transcriptional activity. Thus, technical variation is the only source of variation.

span.label: droplet digital PCR on eight genes in Jurkat cells, against the RNA copy number measured in bulk from the same cell type
span.note: eliminates: naked spike-in RNA standing in for a real transcript inside a real cell - ERCC molecules are not lysed out of anything, and could convert at a different rate · outcome: held
span.quote: Additionally, we estimated the conversion rate of cell transcripts in Jurkat cells by droplet digital PCR (ddPCR). The amount of cDNA of eight genes obtained from single cells after reverse transcription in GEMs was compared with the expected RNA inferred from bulk profiling. The conversion rates among eight genes were between 2.5 and 25.5%, which is consistent with the ERCC data (Supplementary Methods and Supplementary Fig. 2e).

span.label: 293T-only and Jurkat-only samples run through the identical PCA, alongside the mixed ones
span.note: eliminates: the clustering method itself as the source of the two clusters - a procedure that splits a pure sample would have produced the same picture from nothing · outcome: held
span.quote: In contrast, PC1 did not separate cells into two clusters in the 293T- and the Jurkat-only samples (Fig. 2e). Furthermore, in the sample with 1% 293T and 99% Jurkat cells, the number of cells in each of the two clusters was observed at the expected ratio (Fig. 2e, Supplementary Fig. 4a and Supplementary Fig. 4b). A similar trend was observed for 12 independent samples where 293T and Jurkat cells were mixed at five different proportions, demonstrating the system's ability to perform unbiased detection of rare single cells (Supplementary Fig. 4a).

span.label: cell identity assigned a second time from SNVs alone, independently of any marker gene, and compared cell by cell with the marker-based assignment
span.note: eliminates: the choice of marker genes as the source of the cluster identities - genotype and expression are different measurements and could have disagreed · outcome: held
span.quote: In the 1:1 mixed sample, 45% 293T cells primarily (96%) harbored 293T-enriched SNVs, whereas 50% Jurkat cells primarily (94%) harbored Jurkat-enriched SNVs (Fig. 2f and Supplementary Data 2). Jurkat and 293T cells inferred from marker-based analysis are 99% consistent with SNV-based assignment.

span.label: in silico mixing of two donors' reads at 12 ratios from 0 to 50%, where the true label of every cell is known, with sensitivity and PPV computed against it
span.note: eliminates: a detection limit asserted rather than measured - the floor is found by mixing downward until the method stops recovering the minor population · outcome: held
span.quote: Our method was able to identify minor genotypes as low as 3% at >95% sensitivity and PPV (Fig. 4a,b). A minor population could not be detected when the mixed ratio was below 3%

span.label: the same two donors mixed in vitro at 50:50, 90:10 and 99:1 before sequencing, rather than mixed computationally afterwards
span.note: eliminates: in silico mixing as the reason the floor holds - reads combined by arithmetic never pass through a shared droplet, a shared PCR or a shared flow cell · outcome: held
span.quote: We further validated the performance of the method in experiments where PBMCs from Donors B and C were mixed at three ratios, 50:50, 90:10 and 99:1, before scRNA-seq. In the 50:50 mixture sample, cells from Donors B and C were almost indistinguishable by RNA expression (Supplementary Fig. 9d,e). However, they can be separated by their genotype at the correct proportion (Table 1). In addition, the genotype overlap between genotype group 1 and Donor C is 94%, whereas the overlap between genotype group 1 and Donor B is only 63%, both within the range of positive and negative controls, suggesting that group 1 comes from Donor C (Supplementary Methods and Table 1). Similarly, genotype group 2 was inferred to be from Donor B (Supplementary Methods and Table 1). The proportions of the minor genotype were accurately predicted at the 90:10 mixing ratio. Consistent with the in silico mixing results, the minor population could not be detected when B and C were mixed at 99:1 ratio (Table 1).

span.label: 11 pairwise genotype comparisons between samples from the same individual and 15 between different individuals, computed before any patient sample was interpreted
span.note: eliminates: reading a genotype-overlap percentage with no scale - 97% and 78% are host and donor only because the same-individual and different-individual ranges exist · outcome: held
span.quote: To obtain some baseline for the % genotype overlap among different individuals, we performed pairwise comparison of genotypes called from the same individuals (11 pairwise comparisons) or from different individuals (15 pairwise comparisons). The per cent genotype overlap between the same individuals averages ∼98±0.3%, whereas the per cent genotype overlap between the different individuals averages ∼73±2%.

span.label: the routine clinical chimerism assay, PowerPlex 16 on a genetic analyser, run on the same post-transplant samples
span.note: eliminates: the new method being its own witness - the chimerism call is checked against the assay currently trusted for that decision, in both patients · outcome: held
span.quote: This observation is consistent with the clinical chimerism assay, which demonstrated only 12% donor in the post-transplant sample. In contrast, SNV analysis on the post-HSCT sample from AML035 did not detect the presence of two genotype groups. The sample only shared 78% similarity with AML035 host cells, suggesting that the post-HSCT sample was all donor-derived (Table 2). This finding was validated by the independent clinical chimerism assay.

span.label: the remaining fresh PBMCs from the same donor frozen and re-run three weeks later, compared with the fresh library gene by gene and cluster by cluster
span.note: eliminates: freeze-thaw as an explanation of any composition difference in the frozen repository specimens the method is meant to be used on · outcome: held
span.quote: To determine the effect that a freeze-thaw might have on gene expression and thus on the ability of our scRNA-seq pipeline to classify cell type in frozen repository specimens, we froze the remaining fresh PBMCs from Donor A, and made a scRNA-seq library from gently thawed cells 3 weeks later where ∼3k cells were recovered (Supplementary Methods). The two data sets (fresh and frozen) showed a high similarity between their average gene expression (r=0.96; Supplementary Methods and Supplementary Fig. 8a).

span.label: ten bead-enriched, separately profiled subpopulations of PBMCs from the same donor, each clustered on its own and checked against FACS
span.note: eliminates: substructure being an artefact of clustering a mixed population - a purified sample that splits would indict the pipeline, and most of them did not split · outcome: held
span.quote: Clustering analysis revealed a lack of substructure in most samples, consistent with the samples being homogenous populations, and in agreement with FACS analysis (Supplementary Methods and Supplementary Figs 6 and 7).

span.label: Seurat, an independently written clustering package, run on the same 68k gene-barcode matrix
span.note: eliminates: the cell-type structure being specific to the authors' own PCA and k-means choices - a second package agreeing on some boundaries and not others locates which ones the data supports · outcome: partial
span.quote: We have also tried to cluster the 68k PBMC data with Seurat (Supplementary Methods). While it was able to distinguish inferred CD4+ naive from inferred CD8+ naive T cells, it was not able to cleanly separate out inferred activated cytotoxic T cells from inferred NK cells (Supplementary Fig. 5i). Such populations have overlapping functions, making separation at the transcriptome level particularly difficult and even unexpected.

span.label: GEM
span.quote: The core of the technology is a Gel bead in EMulsion (GEM). GEM generation takes place in an 8-channel microfluidic chip that encapsulates single gel beads at ∼80% fill rate (Fig. 1a–c). Each gel bead is functionalized with barcoded oligonucleotides that consists of: (i) sequencing adapters and primers, (ii) a 14 bp barcode drawn from ∼750,000 designed sequences to index GEMs, (iii) a 10 bp randomer to index molecules (unique molecular identifier, UMI) and (iv) an anchored 30 bp oligo-dT to prime polyadenylated RNA transcripts (Fig. 1d).

span.label: UMI
span.quote: The core of the technology is a Gel bead in EMulsion (GEM). GEM generation takes place in an 8-channel microfluidic chip that encapsulates single gel beads at ∼80% fill rate (Fig. 1a–c). Each gel bead is functionalized with barcoded oligonucleotides that consists of: (i) sequencing adapters and primers, (ii) a 14 bp barcode drawn from ∼750,000 designed sequences to index GEMs, (iii) a 10 bp randomer to index molecules (unique molecular identifier, UMI) and (iv) an anchored 30 bp oligo-dT to prime polyadenylated RNA transcripts (Fig. 1d).

span.label: multiplet rate
span.quote: Eight cell-containing GEMs had a substantial fraction of human and mouse UMI counts (the UMI count is >1% of each species' UMI count distribution), yielding an inferred multiplet rate (rate of GEMs containing >1 cell) of 1.6%

span.label: multiplets
span.quote: Cells in cluster 10 express markers of B, T and dendritic cells, suggesting a likely cluster of multiplets (Fig. 3b,c). The size of the cluster suggests the multiplets comprises mostly B:dendritic and B:T:dendritic cells (Supplementary Methods). With ∼9k cells recovered per channel, we expect a ∼9% multiplet rate and that the majority of multiplets would only contain T cells. More sophisticated methods will be required to detect multiplets from identical or highly similar cell types.

span.label: cell capture rate
span.quote: In addition, we observed ∼50% cell capture rate, which is the ratio of the number of cells detected by sequencing and the number of cells loaded. The capture rate is consistent across four types of cells with cell loads ranging from ∼1,000 to ∼23,000 (Supplementary Table 2), a key improvement over some existing scRNA-seq methods.

span.label: cross-talk
span.quote: Last, the mean fraction of UMI counts from the other species was 0.9% in both human and mouse GEMs, indicating a low level of cross-talk between cell barcodes (Online Supplementary Methods).

span.label: technical variation
span.quote: The ERCC experiments also allowed us to estimate the relative proportion of biological and technical variation. Since ERCCs are in solution, they do not introduce biological variation related to differences in cell size, RNA content or transcriptional activity. Thus, technical variation is the only source of variation.

span.label: biological variation
span.quote: The ERCC experiments also allowed us to estimate the relative proportion of biological and technical variation. Since ERCCs are in solution, they do not introduce biological variation related to differences in cell size, RNA content or transcriptional activity. Thus, technical variation is the only source of variation.

span.label: ERCC
span.quote: We also directly measured cDNA conversion rate by loading External RNA Controls Consortium (ERCC) synthetic RNAs into GEMs in place of cells. We found that mean UMI counts from sequencing was highly correlated (r=0.96) with molecule counts calculated from the loading concentration of ERCC (Fig. 2d and Supplementary Fig. 2a).

span.label: SNVs
span.quote: While previous studies have used existing SNVs from DNA sequencing or large-scale copy number changes in the transcriptome data to distinguish cells by genotype, these methods cannot be applied to transplant samples where donor and host genotype is not known a priori, and when donor and host are closely matched in genotype.

span.label: chimerism
span.quote: Current clinical chimerism tests have a number of limitations, namely (1) the flow-sorted cell populations are limited by cell surface markers, (2) only populations with sufficient cell counts can be used for PCR assays and (3) they are not intended for the detection of minimal residual disease. Here we present a simple method that addresses these limitations, resolves host and donor chimerism at single-cell resolution and enables extensive characterization of cell subtypes by integrating scRNA-seq with de novo SNV calling.

span.label: genotype overlap
span.quote: To obtain some baseline for the % genotype overlap among different individuals, we performed pairwise comparison of genotypes called from the same individuals (11 pairwise comparisons) or from different individuals (15 pairwise comparisons). The per cent genotype overlap between the same individuals averages ∼98±0.3%, whereas the per cent genotype overlap between the different individuals averages ∼73±2%.

span.label: Seurat
span.quote: We have also tried to cluster the 68k PBMC data with Seurat (Supplementary Methods). While it was able to distinguish inferred CD4+ naive from inferred CD8+ naive T cells, it was not able to cleanly separate out inferred activated cytotoxic T cells from inferred NK cells (Supplementary Fig. 5i). Such populations have overlapping functions, making separation at the transcriptome level particularly difficult and even unexpected.

span.label: Poisson distribution
span.quote: The results indicate an approximate adherence to a Poisson distribution. However, the percentage of multiple cell encapsulations was 16% higher than the expected value, possibly due to subsampling error or to cell–cell interactions (some two-cell clumps were observed during the manual count) (Supplementary Fig. 1b).

span.label: multiplet rate - AS MEASURED BY SPECIES MIXING: twice the share of barcodes carrying significant UMI counts from both genomes, which can only see cross-species doublets
span.quote: In the mouse and human mixing experiments, multiplet rate was defined as twice the rate of cell barcodes with significant UMI counts from both mouse and human, where top 1% of UMI counts was considered significant. The extent of barcode crosstalk was assessed by the fraction of mouse reads in human barcodes, or vice versa.

span.label: multiplet rate - AS MEASURED BY SNV: twice the share of cells whose SNV counts fall between the two cell lines, which still cannot see a doublet of two like cells
span.quote: Cells were labelled as Jurkat or 293T based on Jurkat- and 293T-specific SNV counts, where the fraction of counts from the other species is <0.2. Cells with a fraction of SNV from either species between 0.2 and 0.8 are considered multiplets. The inferred multiplet rate is 2* observed multiplet rate (to account for Jurkat:Jurkat and 293T:293T multiplets).

span.label: the method's level of detection - AS STATED IN RESULTS: 3%, with minor genotypes identified at >95% sensitivity and PPV and nothing recovered below it
span.quote: Our method was able to identify minor genotypes as low as 3% at >95% sensitivity and PPV (Fig. 4a,b). A minor population could not be detected when the mixed ratio was below 3%

span.label: the method's level of detection - AS STATED IN METHODS: 4% of 6,000 cells, from the same in silico mixing experiment; the paper never reconciles the two
span.quote: Selecting K=1 indicates that the mixture fraction is below the level of detection of the method, which in in silico mixing experiments was determined to be 4% of 6,000 cells.

span.label: variation in UMI counts - IN A DROPLET HOLDING A CELL: biological and technical together, CV2 ~11-19%
span.quote: The squared CV (CV2) is ∼7% among all the ERCC experiments. In comparison, CV2 in samples of mouse and human cells is ∼11–19% (Supplementary Fig. 1d), suggesting that technical variance accounts for ∼50% of total variance, consistent with the observations from Klein et al.

span.label: variation in UMI counts - IN A DROPLET HOLDING SYNTHETIC RNA: technical only, by construction, CV2 ~7%
span.quote: The ERCC experiments also allowed us to estimate the relative proportion of biological and technical variation. Since ERCCs are in solution, they do not introduce biological variation related to differences in cell size, RNA content or transcriptional activity. Thus, technical variation is the only source of variation.

span.label: critiques → existing scRNA-seq methods - microfluidic approaches with limited throughput, plate methods needing FACS into many plates, and droplet methods requiring custom devices and reagents
span.quote: However, previously described scRNA-seq methods face practical challenges when scaling to tens of thousands of cells or when it is necessary to capture as many cells as possible from a limited sample. Commercially available, microfluidic-based approaches have limited throughput. Plate-based methods often require time-consuming fluorescence-activated cell sorting (FACS) into many plates that must be processed separately. Droplet-based techniques have enabled processing of tens of thousands of cells in a single experiment, but current approaches require generation of custom microfluidic devices and reagents.

span.label: critiques → clinical chimerism testing by PCR on flow-sorted populations, which is bounded by cell-surface markers, needs sufficient cell counts per population, and is not intended to detect minimal residual disease
span.quote: Current clinical chimerism tests have a number of limitations, namely (1) the flow-sorted cell populations are limited by cell surface markers, (2) only populations with sufficient cell counts can be used for PCR assays and (3) they are not intended for the detection of minimal residual disease. Here we present a simple method that addresses these limitations, resolves host and donor chimerism at single-cell resolution and enables extensive characterization of cell subtypes by integrating scRNA-seq with de novo SNV calling.

span.label: extends → genotype-based cell assignment, by inferring both genomes de novo from the transcriptome rather than requiring DNA sequencing or large copy-number changes known in advance
span.quote: While previous studies have used existing SNVs from DNA sequencing or large-scale copy number changes in the transcriptome data to distinguish cells by genotype, these methods cannot be applied to transplant samples where donor and host genotype is not known a priori, and when donor and host are closely matched in genotype.

span.label: confirms → Klein et al.'s estimate that technical variance accounts for about half of the total variance in droplet scRNA-seq
span.quote: The squared CV (CV2) is ∼7% among all the ERCC experiments. In comparison, CV2 in samples of mouse and human cells is ∼11–19% (Supplementary Fig. 1d), suggesting that technical variance accounts for ∼50% of total variance, consistent with the observations from Klein et al.

span.label: qualifies → its own PBMC classification - the correlation-based assignment blurs T-cell subpopulation boundaries, and an independent package fails on a different pair
span.quote: We have also tried to cluster the 68k PBMC data with Seurat (Supplementary Methods). While it was able to distinguish inferred CD4+ naive from inferred CD8+ naive T cells, it was not able to cleanly separate out inferred activated cytotoxic T cells from inferred NK cells (Supplementary Fig. 5i). Such populations have overlapping functions, making separation at the transcriptome level particularly difficult and even unexpected.

span.label: technical variation —distinct-from→ biological variation
span.note: differs in: whether the source of the variance is the cell or the instrument · the relation itself is separately evidenced · strength of the relation: 0.95
span.quote: The ERCC experiments also allowed us to estimate the relative proportion of biological and technical variation. Since ERCCs are in solution, they do not introduce biological variation related to differences in cell size, RNA content or transcriptional activity. Thus, technical variation is the only source of variation.

span.label: multiplet rate —operationalised-as→ UMI

span.quote: The core of the technology is a Gel bead in EMulsion (GEM). GEM generation takes place in an 8-channel microfluidic chip that encapsulates single gel beads at ∼80% fill rate (Fig. 1a–c). span.label: technical variation
span.quote: The ERCC experiments also allowed us to estimate the relative proportion of biological and technical variation. Since ERCCs are in solution, they do not introduce biological variation related to differences in cell size, RNA content or transcriptional activity. Thus, technical variation is the only source of variation.
